growing_specifications.description: High-value culinary Solanaceous fruit vegetable widely grown across Ilocos, Bukidnon, Nueva Ecija, and backyard gardens in the Philippines. Sensitive to waterlogging and requires vertical bamboo support (tulos) to prevent fruit rotting.

category_why.title: Why is Tomato classified under Solanaceous / Fruit?
category_why.summary: Tomato belongs to the botanical family Solanaceae (nightshade family). It develops from flower ovaries into fleshy berries with internal seed locules and exhibits distinct upright branching growth habits.
points: Nightshade Family Genetics: Shares botanical traits with eggplant and chili peppers, thriving in warm tropical weather while requiring protection from solanaceous pests like whiteflies and fruit borers.
Fleshy Berry Morphology: True botanical berry composed of a smooth outer pericarp, succulent placenta, and multiple seed cavities rich in antioxidant lycopene and vitamin C.
Branching & Trellis Habit: Produces vigorous vegetative side-shoots (suckers) at leaf axils that demand pruning and vertical bamboo staking (tulos) to elevate fruit above damp soil.

harvest_why.title: Why is the harvest maturity set to 60–72 days?
harvest_why.summary: Commercial harvesting at 60–72 days captures firm, high-flavor fruits at the breaker to pink-red stage, ensuring maximum market shelf life and preventing cracking.
points: Germination & Nursery Phase (Days 1–18): Seeds emerge within 4–5 days; seedlings develop 4–5 sturdy true leaves in nursery trays before field transplanting.
Vegetative Staking Phase (Days 19–38): Intensive root establishment and upward stem expansion; sturdy bamboo stakes are installed before flower cluster initiation.
Anthesis & Fruit Set (Days 39–54): Yellow flower clusters open; gentle air movement or manual stake shaking promotes pollination and rapid fruit cell expansion.
Breaker to Red Ripe Window (Days 55–72): Fruits transition from green to breaker (pink blush at blossom end) and uniform red. Early morning hand-harvesting keeps fruits cool and firm.

watering_why.title: Why does Tomato need watering every 2 days?
watering_why.summary: Tomatoes require consistent root-zone moisture to transport calcium efficiently, preventing fatal blossom end rot while avoiding waterlogging that invites bacterial wilt.
points: Blossom End Rot Prevention: Calcium is delivered strictly via active transpiration. Drying out soil for 3 or more days abruptly halts calcium transport to developing fruit tips, causing sunken black rot.

Root Aeration & Bacterial Wilt Defense: Daily waterlogging creates anaerobic soil conditions favored by Ralstonia solanacearum (Bacterial Wilt). A 2-day furrow or basin irrigation cycle maintains optimal 60–70% field moisture capacity.
Soil-Level Irrigation: Applying water directly to the root zone without wetting canopy foliage prevents fungal spore germination of Early Blight (Alternaria) and Bacterial Spot.

soil_why.title: Why does Tomato require pH 6.0–6.8 and Loam / Sandy Loam?
soil_why.summary: A slightly acidic to neutral root zone optimizes phosphorus and calcium bioavailability essential for continuous blossom retention and thick fruit wall formation.
points: Optimum Nutrient Solubility: At pH 6.0–6.8, soil phosphorus, potassium, and calcium remain bioavailable for active uptake by fine fibrous feeder roots.
Soil Aeration & Fast Drainage: Loam or sandy loam enriched with decomposed organic compost and carbonized rice hull (CRH) provides rapid infiltration during heavy tropical rainstorms.

varieties.disease_resistance: High resistance to Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV) and Bacterial Wilt
varieties.description: Premier commercial hybrid developed by East-West Seed. High-yielding determinate cultivar producing firm, thick-walled oval fruits with exceptional transport durability for both wet and dry season Philippine markets.

varieties.disease_resistance: Moderate heat tolerance and Bacterial Wilt resistance; traditional seed-saving variety
varieties.description: Lowland open-pollinated release bred by UPLB Institute of Plant Breeding (IPB). Produces juicy, deep red fruits ideal for household gardens and local wet markets during the dry season.

varieties.disease_resistance: Tolerance to Fusarium Wilt and Root-knot Nematodes
varieties.description: Widely planted hybrid in Central and Southern Luzon known for prolific flower cluster setting, uniform bright red ripening, and balanced tart-sweet culinary flavor.
